questions.stem: HARSHA VARDHANA was the ruler of which dynasty in the early 7th century?

options.option_text: Gupta dynasty, the golden-age dynasty
Pushyabhuti (Vardhana) dynasty of Thanesar
Pala dynasty of eastern Bengal area
Chola dynasty of southern Tamil region

questions.explanation: Harsha (r. 606-647 CE) — Pushyabhuti / VARDHANA dynasty, capital initially at THANESAR (Haryana), shifted to KANAUJ. Came to throne after his elder brother Rajya Vardhana was killed by Sasanka of Gauda. United north India after the post-Gupta fragmentation. Was DEFEATED by PULAKESIN II (Chalukya of Vatapi) at Narmada (~630 CE) — limit of his southern advance. Distractor 1 — Guptas declined ~550 CE. Distractor 3 — Palas were ~750-1150. Distractor 4 — Cholas were southern.

questions.stem: The Chinese pilgrim HIUEN TSANG (Xuanzang) visited India during the reign of:

options.option_text: Chandragupta II, the Gupta emperor
Harsha Vardhana, between 629 and 645 CE
Akbar, the Mughal emperor of 16th century
Ashoka, the Mauryan emperor of 3rd c. BCE

questions.explanation: HIUEN TSANG / Xuanzang (~602-664 CE) — Chinese Buddhist monk; visited India 629-645 CE, much of it during Harsha's reign. Studied at NALANDA university (~5 years). Wrote 'Si-Yu-Ki' (Records of the Western Regions). Praised Harsha's administration; described religious assemblies he attended (the famous Kanauj assembly + Prayag Mahamoksha Parishad — held every 5 years, where Harsha donated his wealth). Distractor 1 = Fa-Hien visited Chandragupta II's reign (~405 CE). Distractor 3, 4 — anachronistic.

questions.stem: BANABHATTA was the COURT POET of Harsha, famous for writing:

options.option_text: Mricchakatika, the famous play of love
Harshacharita and Kadambari (in Sanskrit)
Mudrarakshasa, a political play of Maurya
Akbarnama, the chronicle of Akbar's reign

questions.explanation: BANABHATTA — court poet of Harsha, late 7th c. CE. Wrote: (1) HARSHACHARITA — biography of Harsha, first 8 cantos, in Sanskrit prose (PROSE-POEM, gadya-kavya). One of India's earliest historical biographies. (2) KADAMBARI — Sanskrit romance novel; one of the world's earliest novels. Distractor 1 = Mricchakatika, by Shudraka (~ 5th c., Gupta period). Distractor 3 = Mudrarakshasa, by Vishakhadatta (Gupta period). Distractor 4 = Akbarnama by Abul Fazl (Mughal).

questions.stem: Harsha was DEFEATED by which southern emperor at the Narmada around 630 CE?

options.option_text: Krishnadeva Raya, the Vijayanagara emperor
Pulakesin II, of the Chalukya dynasty (Vatapi)
Rajaraja Chola, the great Chola emperor
Nrip Tunga, the Rashtrakuta emperor

questions.explanation: Pulakesin II (r. 610-642 CE) — greatest Chalukya king of Vatapi (modern Badami, Karnataka). Defeated Harsha at the BANKS OF NARMADA (~630 CE) → halted Harsha's southward advance. Pulakesin's Aihole inscription (composed by RAVIKIRTI) celebrates his victory + other achievements. Pulakesin received an embassy from Khusrau II of Persia. Was eventually defeated + killed by NARASIMHAVARMAN I (Pallava king) ~642 CE. Distractor 1 — Vijayanagara was 14-16th c. Distractor 3 — Chola peak was 11th c. Distractor 4 — Rashtrakutas came after Chalukyas.

questions.stem: Harsha shifted his capital from Thanesar to:

options.option_text: Pataliputra, the old Mauryan capital
Kanauj (Kanyakubja), in present-day UP
Ujjain, an ancient cultural centre
Tamralipti, an ancient port city

questions.explanation: Harsha shifted his capital to KANAUJ / Kanyakubja (modern Kannauj, UP) — strategic location commanding the Doab. Inherited from his sister Rajyashri's husband (Maukhari king Grahavarman, killed by Sasanka). Kanauj remained politically important for centuries — TRIPARTITE STRUGGLE (8th-9th c.) between Pratiharas, Palas, Rashtrakutas was over Kanauj. Distractor 1 = Pataliputra (Mauryan/Gupta). Distractor 3 = Ujjain (Avanti, also a notable ancient city, but not Harsha's). Distractor 4 = Tamralipti (port in Bengal, Mauryan-Gupta era).

questions.stem: Harsha was a generous patron of which religion in his later years?

options.option_text: Jainism, the ahimsa-focused Indian tradition
Mahayana Buddhism, under Hiuen Tsang's influence
Zoroastrianism, the Persian Parsi religion
Christianity, with an early Indian connection

questions.explanation: Harsha — initially follower of Shaivism (his earlier inscriptions), later turned to MAHAYANA BUDDHISM under Hiuen Tsang's influence. Held the famous KANAUJ ASSEMBLY (643 CE) to honour Mahayana Buddhism — 18 days, attended by Hiuen Tsang as chief of the Mahayana school. Held PRAYAG MAHAMOKSHA PARISHAD every 5 years at Allahabad — donated his wealth (alms to monks, Brahmins, the poor). Plays attributed to Harsha himself: NAGANANDA (Buddhist, plot from Jataka), PRIYADARSIKA, RATNAVALI (Sanskrit love-comedies). Tolerant patron — supported Hinduism + Jainism too.

questions.stem: After Harsha died (647 CE) without an heir, his minister Arjuna usurped the throne but was defeated by:

options.option_text: Pulakesin II of the Chalukya dynasty
A Tibet-Chinese expedition under Wang Xuance
Khusrau II of the Persian Sassanid empire
Bhaskaravarman of the Kamarupa dynasty

questions.explanation: WANG XUANCE — Chinese envoy from Tang court (visiting newly-vacant Harsha's court). Arjuna (the usurper) attacked the Chinese embassy + killed many. Wang escaped to Nepal + Tibet, raised an army (Tibetan king Songtsen Gampo's troops + Nepalese), returned, defeated Arjuna, captured him, took him back to China as prisoner. UNUSUAL military intervention from China in north India. Bhaskaravarman of Kamarupa (Assam) was Harsha's ally + was given an honorary territory after Harsha's death; he was a contemporary, not the conqueror of Arjuna.
